we developed a novel approach to recover complete or near-complete genomes from metagenomic datasets, that we recovered complete and near-complete genomes of uncultivated bacteria from metagenomic data from a bioreactor and that we showed that our approach is better than other methods for the recovery of genomes from metagenomes.

we present an approach to recover high quality microbial genomes from deeply-sequenced metagenomes and that this approach facilitates recovery of more accurate genome bins than currently used methods, based on sequence composition.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods to obtain high quality genome sequences of rare microorganisms.
the recovery of high-quality microbial genomes directly from metagenomes, and in particular, genomes of rare species.
the recovery of microbial genomes from metagenomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors present an interesting approach to recover genomes from metagenomes, which is not limited to the use of sequence composition.
the method of differential coverage binning, which was developed and used in this work, is a powerful tool for recovering high-quality genome bins of rare species.
the approach presented in this paper, differential coverage binning, is a powerful method to obtain genome sequences for rare species from complex communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to obtain high-quality genomes from metagenomic data.
we have developed an efficient and effective method to recover genomes of uncultivated bacteria from metagenomes.
we developed a new approach to assemble high-quality genomes from multiple metagenomes and applied the approach to assemble genomes for 12 rare bacteria from the activated sludge bioprocess.
The main takeaway from our work is that
differential coverage binners are able to produce more complete and higher-quality genomes than other binning methods, which are typically sequence composition–based.
the recovery of high-quality microbial genomes is possible from deeply sequenced environmental metagenomes, even for rare species.
differential coverage binners (DCB) can recover high quality genome bins from complex metagenomes.
